learningObjectives.title: The importance of water in the diet
Functions of water in the body

questions.q: Approximately what proportion of an adult's body weight is made up of water?
questions.explain: Water makes up around two-thirds (roughly 60%) of an adult's body weight, showing how essential it is.

questions.q: What is the commonly recommended daily fluid intake for an adult?
questions.explain: Around 6-8 glasses (about 1.5-2 litres) of fluid a day is recommended to stay properly hydrated.

questions.q: Which body function does water carry out through sweating?
questions.explain: Water helps regulate body temperature because sweat evaporates from the skin and cools the body down.

questions.q: Water forms the main part of which body fluid that transports nutrients and oxygen?
questions.explain: Water is the main component of blood, which transports nutrients and oxygen around the body.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common sign of dehydration?
questions.explain: Dark, concentrated urine is a key sign that the body is short of water and becoming dehydrated.

questions.q: Water is lost from the body mainly through which of the following?
questions.explain: The body loses water through urine, sweat, breathing (and faeces), so it must be replaced regularly.

questions.q: In which form does water help remove waste products from the body?
questions.explain: Water enables the kidneys to remove waste products from the blood and excrete them as urine.

questions.q: Why do foods such as fruit and vegetables contribute to daily water intake?
options: They have a high water content
questions.explain: Many fruits and vegetables have a high water content, so eating them adds to overall fluid intake.

questions.q: Why is water important for digestion?
options: It provides energy for the gut
It acts as a medium for chemical reactions and helps move food through the gut
It replaces the need for fibre
It hardens food in the stomach
questions.explain: Water is the medium in which digestive reactions take place and it helps food move smoothly through the digestive system.

questions.q: Why does urine become darker when a person is dehydrated?
options: There is less water to dilute the waste, so it becomes more concentrated
The body adds extra colour to it
questions.explain: With less water available, the waste in urine is more concentrated, making the urine darker in colour.

questions.q: How does water help protect the joints in the body?
options: By acting as a lubricant to reduce friction
questions.explain: Water helps lubricate joints, allowing them to move smoothly and reducing friction between surfaces.

questions.q: Why should fluid intake be increased during hot weather?
options: Because more water is lost through sweating
Because the body needs less energy
questions.explain: In hot weather the body sweats more to stay cool, so extra fluid is needed to replace the water lost.

questions.q: Why can drinking too little water lead to constipation?
options: Water is needed to keep the contents of the bowel soft and moving
Water removes all fibre from food
Water stops the gut absorbing nutrients
questions.explain: Without enough water the contents of the bowel become hard and difficult to pass, causing constipation.

questions.q: How does sweating help cool the body down?
options: As sweat evaporates from the skin it takes heat with it
questions.explain: When sweat evaporates from the skin's surface it removes heat, helping to lower body temperature.

questions.q: A footballer has just finished a match on a hot day and feels very thirsty. What is the best choice to rehydrate?
options: No drink until the next meal
questions.explain: Water is the best choice to replace fluid lost through sweat and quickly rehydrate the body.

questions.q: A pupil complains of a headache, tiredness and has dark urine after a busy day with few drinks. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explain: Headache, tiredness and dark urine after drinking little are classic signs of dehydration.

questions.q: An elderly person often forgets to drink and feels dizzy. Which advice best helps maintain their hydration?
options: Only drink at mealtimes once a day
Sip drinks regularly throughout the day
Avoid all fluids to reduce trips to the toilet
Replace all drinks with dry snacks
questions.explain: Drinking small amounts regularly throughout the day helps maintain hydration, especially for those who forget to drink.

questions.q: A cook wants to plan a lunch that helps boost the family's fluid intake. Which addition would help most?
options: A bowl of soup and salad
questions.explain: Soup and salad have a high water content, so they add usefully to the family's daily fluid intake.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Home Economics: Food and Nutrition (2017) specification; Water
